explanations: Incorrect. Combining unreconciled answers produces a long document that still contains whatever gaps and conflicts the originals had.
Correct. A comparison is only as good as its frame. Fixing the rows and columns first is what stops the result being shaped by whatever happened to come up in earlier chats.
Incorrect. Format is a downstream decision; choosing it before the content is defined locks in a shape that may not fit.
Incorrect. A ranking produced before the criteria are agreed reflects unstated assumptions she cannot inspect or defend.
options: A) Ask Claude to combine all of the earlier answers into one long document she can read through.
B) Agree which suppliers and which criteria belong in the comparison before asking for any output.
C) Choose the output format now, so that every further answer can be produced in that same shape.
D) Ask Claude to rank the six suppliers straight away and work backwards from the ranking it gives.
question: A manager needs a comparison of six suppliers across five criteria. The information is currently spread across several separate Claude answers. What should she do first?
